question.value: Do SiO (5-4) clumps inside the circumnuclear ring around Sgr A* trace protostellar outflows, indicating ongoing massive star formation near the black hole?

evidence.quote: The SiO clumps are interpreted as highly embedded protostellar outflows, signifying an early stage of massive star formation near Sgr A\* in the last $10^4-10^5$ years.

results_numeric.quantity: Number of SiO (5-4) clumps within 0.6 pc of Sgr A*

evidence.quote: detection of 11 SiO (5-4) clumps of molecular gas within 0.6pc (15$''$) of Sgr A\*
The column densities of SiO for Clumps 1 and 11 are estimated to be N(SiO)$\sim8.6\times10^{13}$ and $\sim1.3\times10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$, respectively.
the gas density of hydrogen nuclei is constrained to n$_{\rm H_2}\sim (3-9)\times10^5$ cm$^{-3}$ within a temperature range 100-200K.
SiO abundance of 5.6$\times10^{-10}$ which is clearly much higher than is expected in quiescent molecular clouds.
the velocity gradient is estimated to be 833 and 165 km s$^{-1}$  pc$^{-1}$ for clumps with broad ($\sim50$ km s$^{-1}$) and narrow ($\sim10$ km s$^{-1}$) linewidths respectively.
we derive masses of $34.3\pm5.9$ and 19.4$\pm2.5$

findings_qualitative.value: Three SiO clumps nearest Sgr A* have the broadest, most asymmetric lines; others lie mainly NE of the mini-spiral with narrow lines

evidence.quote: The remaining clumps, distributed mainly to the NE of the ionized mini-spiral, have narrow FWZI ($\sim18-56$ km s$^{-1}$).

claims.hypothesis: SiO clumps inside the ring are protostellar outflows
claims.experiment: Gaussian line fits, LVG with CARMA SiO (2-1), boundedness test, luminosity-FWZI comparison with YSO samples
claims.result: Clumps unbound by self-gravity; luminosities between low- and high-mass YSOs; abundance high
claims.finding: Clumps trace YSO outflows, i.e. ongoing massive star formation near Sgr A*

evidence.quote: all point to the conclusion that these clumps are tracing YSOs with protostellar outflows.

claims.hypothesis: YSO candidates are associated with SiO clumps
claims.experiment: SED fits of IR sources near clumps 1 and 3
claims.result: Two YSO candidates with masses ~34 and ~19 Msun

evidence.quote: We identified two new YSO candidates in the N arm near Clumps 1 and 3.

claims.hypothesis: Radiation pressure or clump collisions can trigger star formation here
claims.result: Radiation pressure gives n~4e8 cm^-3; collisions need ~60 clumps
claims.finding: Both possible; collisions struggle with the number of sources

evidence.quote: thus a population of 60 clumps are needed to produce the number of observed SiO clumps.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Interaction of molecular clumps with N-arm ionized gas considered but kinematics inconsistent

evidence.quote: the kinematics of the molecular and ionized gas are inconsistent with the interaction picture.

limitations_admitted.value: Synthesized beam highly elongated, so a filling factor of 0.5 was chosen

evidence.quote: The synthesized beam is highly elongated in one direction, thus we chose a beam filling factor of 0.5.
